dialog.body: Yeah, hi Kevin, Joel Monteiro here, I'm on Bacheller Street, and I'm actually on hold with another office on my other line right now so if I go quiet that's why, but I've got to tell you, after last weekend's nor'easter, Saturday into Sunday, I got water in my cellar, a few inches, and I've been in this house a lot of years and that has never once happened, never, and the water all collects down at the low end of the street where the drain is, it just sits there and builds up, and now it's running right toward my neighbor's garage, and I want to know is that a city drain or is that a state one, because nobody seems to know and I keep getting passed around.
Okay, wow, that's a lot. Let me get it down. Bacheller Street, water in your cellar, a few inches, and it's pooling at the low end and heading for a neighbor's garage. Did I get that?
That's it, yeah. And it's still wet down there, it's Wednesday, it's been three days.
Yeah, that's too long to be sitting. What's the house number?
362. Three sixty-two Bacheller. The drain I'm talking about is down the end, past the corner, maybe six or seven houses down from me.

Got it. So on the city versus state thing, most of the streets in that neighborhood are city streets, so the drains on them are ours. State only has the bigger roads. Bacheller is a city street, so I'd treat that as ours and get it on the list.
Okay, so it's yours. Then why is it all clogged up? Nobody's been out to clear it, I'd bet. I'm paying taxes here.

I hear you. After a storm like that, the crews have a pile of drain calls, but I'll write this up as water running toward a garage and a cellar already taking water, so it goes up higher in the stack. Let me put it in. Storm drain, low end of Bacheller Street, backing up, water toward a neighbor's garage. Do you know if the grate's covered with leaves or snow, or is it just full?
Leaves and slush, packed in there, and the water just sits over the top of it like a pond.
Okay, leaves and slush on the grate. That helps the crew. Is there a good number to reach you?
401-555-0167, got it. And that's your cell?
Cell, yeah, so it might break up on me. [line breaks up] Hello? Sorry, the other office just came on, hang on a second. No, they're not, it's still the music. Okay, I'm back.
No problem. I've got you down. Somebody from the crew should be out to look at that drain, probably today or tomorrow, and if they can't clear it right away I'll have them call you.
Today or tomorrow. Okay. Because if it freezes tonight that whole street is a skating rink and my cellar is still wet.
Understood. I'll flag the freezing part in the note too.
All right. Thank you, Kevin. Just get somebody down there.
Will do, Joel. You take care.
